Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time earlier. As promised, I attached a lightweight mutual action plan (MAP) seed and a slide skeleton so we can quickly align stakeholders and approval gates. I wanted to share a suggested 45-day evaluation sprint broken into three two-week sprints with clear technical acceptance criteria and procurement decision points.

High-level proposed milestones (quick):
- Week 0: Kickoff + infra readiness (VPC access, sample dataset subset)
- Weeks 1–2: Model integration + baseline perf (latency/cost)
- Weeks 3–4: Feature validation + safety/regression checks (prompt sets)
- Week 5–6: Acceptance testing + procurement/contract signoff

Two asks: can you confirm the procurement timeline (who signs, expected legal review duration) and share a short list of internal stakeholders I should include on the MAP?

Links / attachments: I uploaded a MAP draft (Google Doc) and slide outline — both editable. Also attached a brief pilot scope spreadsheet for technical owners.

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the documents. This looks promising. A few immediate notes:

- Procurement/Legal: our procurement lead is Sara Lim (sara.lim@quantahealth.com). Typical legal review for pilot agreements runs 7–10 business days for small pilots, but it can spike if data handling terms change.

- Stakeholders: include Sara (procurement), Dr. Miguel Alvarez (clinical lead), and our Platform Eng manager (Rita Chen). I can loop them in once we have the MAP link finalized.

Elena / team —

Quick additions from a technical acceptance perspective (added inline to the MAP doc as well):

- Acceptance criteria (minimum): 95th percentile gen latency < 350ms for the baseline prompt set; end-to-end throughput of 10 qps on a single reserved instance during demo window.
- Quality gates: pass rate >= 90% on safety/regression prompt suite (we'll share the suite).
- Canary plan: start on hosted Redwood API, then run a 48–72 hour Dedicated canary if cost/latency tradeoffs demand it (we'll include rollback instructions).

I've updated the slide skeleton with a single-slide "decision gates" visual and added a short appendix for SOC2 artifacts we can provide.
